title: Knight takes the bishop with check, and a pawn takes the knight right back (AI vs AI, real moves)
text:
Two consecutive moves from one AI-vs-AI match: the white knight takes the bishop on d6 with check (Nxd6+), and the black pawn on c7 takes the knight on the same square (cxd6). Both sides are played by the game's own AI; every move is legal and every animation is the engine's own.

Pixel Pawns on the Microsoft Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9PP9G5CQKKZX?cid=rd

title: En passant in a pixel art chess game: the pawn that just moved two squares gets captured, and the capture plays out as a duel
text:
En passant is the chess rule that looks like a bug: a pawn that has just moved two squares can be captured by the enemy pawn beside it, as if it had moved only one square. In Pixel Pawns, our pixel art strategy game, that capture plays out as one of its animated chess battles, with the game's own sound effects. The opening moves (1.e4 c6 2.e5 d5 3.exd6) were set up for this clip, and every move is legal in the real game. Pixel Pawns is offline chess with no ads, with four chess AI levels and hotseat for two players.

Microsoft Store (Windows PC, Xbox): https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9PP9G5CQKKZX
Google Play (Android): https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=hu.bugfactory.pixelpawns
